parts.working_md:
Equation of $\mathrm{PQ}$:

$y=x+c$

$-3=-2+c$

$y=x-1$  $\therefore a=b+1$  ......(1)

From the distance formula:

$7\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{(a-(-2))^{2}+(b-(-3))^{2}}$

$\therefore 98=(a+2)^{2}+(b+3)^{2}$  ......(2)

Subst (1) into (2):

$98=(b+1+2)^{2}+(b+3)^{2}$

$98=b^{2}+6b+9+b^{2}+6b+9$

$0=2b^{2}+12b-80$

$0=b^{2}+6b-40$

$\therefore 0=(b+10)(b-4)$

$\therefore b=4$  (since $b>0$)

Subst $b=4$ into (1):

$\therefore a=4+1=5$

$\therefore \mathrm{P}(5;4)$

$\dfrac{4\cos x(-\sin x)}{\sin(30^{\circ}-x+x)}$

$=\dfrac{-4\sin x\cos x}{\sin 30^{\circ}}$

$=\dfrac{-4\sin x\cos x}{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

$=-8\sin x\cos x$

$=-4(2\sin x\cos x)$

$=-4\sin 2x$

alternatives.working_md:
$\dfrac{4\cos x(-\sin x)}{(\sin 30^{\circ}\cos x-\cos 30^{\circ}\sin x)\cos x+(\cos 30^{\circ}\cos x+\sin 30^{\circ}\sin x)\sin x}$

$=\dfrac{-4\sin x\cos x}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\cos x-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x\right)\cos x+\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin x\right)\sin x}$

$=\dfrac{-2(2\sin x\cos x)}{\dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{2}x+\dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{2}x}$

$=\dfrac{-2(2\sin x\cos x)}{\dfrac{1}{2}(\cos^{2}x+\sin^{2}x)}$

$=\dfrac{-2(2\sin x\cos x)}{\dfrac{1}{2}(1)}$

$=-8\cos x\sin x$

$=-4(2\sin x\cos x)$

$=-4\sin 2x$

parts.working_md:
$\cos 2x-7\cos x-3=0$

$2\cos^{2}x-1-7\cos x-3=0$

$2\cos^{2}x-7\cos x-4=0$

$(2\cos x+1)(\cos x-4)=0$

$\therefore\cos x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$  or  $\cos x=4$  (no solution)

$\therefore x=120^{\circ}+n\cdot 360^{\circ}$  or  $x=240^{\circ}+n\cdot 360^{\circ}$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$
